mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a dental crown to sound hollow when I tap it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in many cases this is entirely normal. Dental crowns are made from materials such as porcelain, zirconia, or metal, which transmit sound differently to natural tooth enamel. The hollow or resonant quality you may notice does not automatically indicate a problem. However, if this sound has changed noticeably, or if you are experiencing any discomfort alongside it, it is sensible to have the crown reviewed by your dentist to rule out any underlying issues such as loose cement or decay beneath the crown.

mainEntity.name: Can a dental crown come loose over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, dental crowns can become loose over time. The dental cement used to bond a crown to the prepared tooth can degrade, particularly if exposed to ongoing chewing forces, temperature changes, or bacterial activity. A loose crown may feel slightly mobile or produce a different sound when tapped. It should be assessed by a dentist promptly, as a loose crown can allow bacteria to access the tooth beneath, increasing the risk of decay or infection.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my crown feels loose or sounds different?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you notice that your crown sounds noticeably different or feels at all mobile, contact your dental practice to arrange an appointment. Avoid eating hard or sticky foods on that side of the mouth in the meantime. Do not attempt to remove or recement the crown yourself. Your dentist will examine the crown, assess the underlying tooth, and determine the most appropriate course of action. In most cases, prompt attention to a loose crown can prevent further complications.

mainEntity.name: How long does a dental crown typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of a dental crown varies depending on the material used, the location of the crown in the mouth, your bite, and how well you maintain your oral hygiene. Generally, crowns can last between 10 and 15 years or longer with proper care. All-ceramic and porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns may be more susceptible to chipping than full metal or zirconia options. Regular dental check-ups are important to monitor the condition of your crown and identify any signs of wear or failure early.

mainEntity.name: Can decay develop under a dental crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, decay can develop beneath a dental crown if bacteria are able to enter through a gap at the crown margin — typically caused by a failing cement seal or gum recession exposing the margin of the crown. This is why maintaining good oral hygiene around the crown margin and attending regular dental check-ups is so important. Decay beneath a crown is not always visible or symptomatic in the early stages, but it can be detected during clinical examination and with the help of dental X-rays.

mainEntity.name: Does a dental crown protect the tooth completely from damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dental crown covers and protects the visible portion of the tooth above the gum line, but it does not provide complete protection from all dental problems. The tooth root remains susceptible to gum disease, decay at the crown margin, and root canal issues. Additionally, the crown itself can chip, crack, or become loose over time. This is why regular dental check-ups and good daily oral hygiene remain important even after a crown has been placed.
